title: Polynomial and graded Rees comparison data on the big fppf site
statement:
Use the universe and small-index convention of [def-weil-size-convention], schemes [def-pc-scheme], categories fibred in groupoids and based functors [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], the ringed big fppf site, quasi-coherent algebra sheaves, local surjections and compatible-family global sections of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], and the quasi-coherent module category: the full subcategory of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over that structure ring cut out by the local-presentation quasi-coherence predicate of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Write $\Gamma$ for compatible section families, with evaluation at each object and the map induced by an algebra morphism. A section of a module mapped to an algebra gives the corresponding compatible ring section. Smooth scheme tests use [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism]. An object represents a smooth test if it is isomorphic in the total category to the image of the identity of such a scheme test.
For a fixed fibred groupoid $\mathcal X/S$ and small $L$, a polynomial system consists, for every quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal B$, of a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal P_L(\mathcal B)$, coefficient map $\mathcal B\to\mathcal P_L(\mathcal B)$, compatible global variables, and ring isomorphisms on smooth affine tests with the polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The chart isomorphisms send coefficients to constants and variables to the correspondingly named variables. A ring isomorphism $\Gamma(\mathcal B)[x_l]\simeq\Gamma(\mathcal P_L(\mathcal B))$ is normalized on each smooth affine chart by coefficientwise evaluation of compatible global sections. For each coefficient algebra map there is a polynomial algebra map given on charts by coefficientwise polynomial mapping. The global isomorphisms are natural for these maps, and these polynomial maps preserve local sheaf surjections.
Now let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $P$ a commutative $k$-algebra, $\mathcal X/\operatorname{Spec}k$ a fibred groupoid, and $p:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ a based morphism, with spectrum as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Pull a base scalar to each test by the existing structural scalar map [def-sfb-stack-scalar-algebra], followed by the structure map into $\mathcal B$. Fix an ideal $I\subseteq P$, a small family $a:J\to P$, a quasi-coherent $\mathcal B$, and a polynomial system for $J$. A Rees presentation consists of quasi-coherent modules $K_m$ with monomorphisms $i_m:K_m\to\mathcal B$ in the full quasi-coherent category, a normalized isomorphism $K_0\simeq\mathcal B$ with $i_0$ its identity in these coordinates, and the following data. On each smooth affine test the $i_m$ are injective and their ranges are exactly $(I\mathcal B_U)^m$. Thus these are precisely the ideal powers, including $K_1=I\mathcal B$, $K_0=\mathcal B$ and $K_{m+1}=K_1K_m$. A quasi-coherent algebra quotient has a locally surjective map from $\mathcal B$ whose affine-chart maps are surjective with kernel $I\mathcal B_U$.
There is a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal R$ with maps $K_m\to\mathcal R$ exhibiting its underlying module as their coproduct. On each smooth affine chart it has a ring isomorphism with the ordinary Rees algebra [def-nagata-rees-algebra] of $I\mathcal B_U$, sending a section of $K_m$ to its specified image times $T^m$. A coefficient map $\mathcal B\to\mathcal R$ is the constant-polynomial inclusion in these chart coordinates. There is a locally surjective algebra map $q:\mathcal P_J(\mathcal B)\to\mathcal R$, with its constant composite equal to the coefficient map, and on smooth affine charts its formula is polynomial evaluation at $a_jT$. These homogeneous-summand and multiplication coordinates specify the grading, its degree-zero identity, and its degree-one generators.
Global sections commute with this coproduct: the induced additive map $\bigoplus_m\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,K_m)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,\mathcal R)$ is bijective, using the existing unit-module identification of Hom with compatible-family sections. An injective ring map $\Gamma(\mathcal R)\to\Gamma(\mathcal B)[T]$ sends each homogeneous module section to its image under $i_m$ times $T^m$. Its image consists exactly of polynomials whose coefficient of degree $m$ is the image of some compatible section of $K_m$. Structural base scalars have compatible global section families. For any such families $b_j$ representing $a_j$, the image of $\Gamma(q)$ under the global polynomial and Rees comparisons is polynomial evaluation at $b_jT$. This is equivalently the finite monomial formula $\sum_\alpha b_\alpha a^\alpha T^{|\alpha|}$. These records prescribe all objects and all comparison maps; they assert no existence and choose no presentation. Ideal inclusions are required only on smooth affine tests and on global sections, not on arbitrary nonflat tests.

lean.note: Records of fully normalized polynomial and Rees comparison data, plus explicit section-evaluation and module-section helpers. These definitions assert no existence and make no choice from a theorem. Rees ideal inclusions use QCoh monos and smooth affine charts, not arbitrary big-site monos. Returned-head repair: imports and reuses CategoryTheory.moduliAlgebraSectionsMap from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.StackFlatScalarSections instead of redeclaring it. The quasi-coherent module category is written inline as the full subcategory of SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent on moduliModuleRings (definitionally the theorem-owned abbrev ModuliQCoh), so the record does not cite the theorem lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction.
